chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will surely punish every group in Islam that submits to the leadership of an unjust, oppressive ruler who is not from Allah, even if that group is pious and God-fearing in their deeds. And I will surely forgive every group in Islam that submits to the leadership of a just Imam who is from Allah, even if that group is oppressive and does evil in their deeds.'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary criterion for divine punishment or forgiveness in Islamic governance according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in Fadail al-Shia, this hadith qudsi establishes the theological primacy of Imamate over individual ritual piety, asserting that the legitimacy of leadership determines the community's ultimate fate. It underscores the Shia doctrine that political and spiritual allegiance to a divinely appointed or unjust ruler directly impacts the efficacy of one's worship, a concept central to the distinction between the Ahl al-Bayt's authority and broader Islamic governance.
